caption:
Oggi a Nieuwegein, in Olanda, al congresso della fusione tra il Partito del lavoro e i GroenLinks.

Abbiamo avuto uno splendido confronto con tre donne di grande ispirazione: Jacinda Ardern, ex premier della Nuova Zelanda, la mia amica Kati Piri e Tamara Tripic.

Grazie dell’invito e della splendida accoglienza, e auguri a Frans Timmermans, il leader di questa nuova formazione: siamo al suo fianco verso le prossime elezioni politiche nei Paesi Bassi, dove dopo due anni di caos, a seguito dell’affermazione dell’estrema destra, gli olandesi possono finalmente voltare pagina con un governo affidabile.
text: There is a big difference between a female leader and a feminist leader because it is useless to have a female prime minister that doesn't fight to improve the life of all other women of the country and we can see that difference in what the government in these two years and a half has done for example by cutting down the funds for children education in a country where we have the lowest rates of women unemployment across the whole European Union and if you ask why well you can see what happens when you cut down the public health system when you cut down welfare we know what happens in Italy all the unpaid care work lies on the shoulder of women and this is why they lag behind in work and also when they want to start a new economic activity so it's useless to have a female prime minister if she doesn't fight to improve the life conditions and work conditions of all other women If anyone tells you that kindness, empathy and optimism in politics is weakness, I utterly reject that If you have chosen to go into politics by default you are a resilient person and if you are focused on the needs of others that is one of the strongest motivations I have ever seen in politics it will get you through many a dark day to choose in this era of strongman leadership kindness and empathy that is an act of courage that is bravery actually I think the biggest achievement of our it was called Women Parliamentarian Network is actually I think that we were the only country in the region that ratified Istanbul Convention without protest without demonstration without opposing anything we united the parliament deeply divided country on that issue like you say this is quite unique this is a Labour Green Congress and I think we are the first in the world where these two parties have decided the members have decided to merge we need to keep these two things together because today it's impossible to have a progressive agenda and also to be a progressive party without keeping together social and climate justice Thank you
